decisions.approvalNote: User selected Option 1: application-owned capability profiles.
decisions.context: The user experience should be one configurable workflow rather than one panel per reference system. The selected boundary must let future reference systems reuse supported interactions without adding renderer branches, while keeping exact-release verification, authorization, policy, runtime support, and execution side effects outside untrusted metadata and UI state.

consequences: Run & Test becomes one select-configure-review-run-results experience driven by verified capabilities.
Workflow descriptors remain inert presentation and validation data; handlers and policy stay application/host owned.
The closed deployment referenceRuntimeKind seam can be replaced by stable handler/profile identities without weakening exact release checks.
Desktop and thin client share behavior and lazy-load only the selected workflow.
options.label: Application-owned capability profiles
options.summary: Add a versioned application-owned workflow catalog that resolves an exact approved release or reviewed plan into supported profiles. One shared UI shell renders a fixed set of bounded reusable interaction primitives—such as form, table, transcript, artifact preview, status, confirmation, and history—and dispatches explicit actions through allowlisted application handlers composed by each host. Existing conversation, data, review, deployment, and execution use cases remain authoritative behind those handlers.
tradeoffs: Requires new contracts, application catalog/handler ports, transport parity, and migration of the current panels into reusable primitives.
Avoids a universal runtime payload while removing reference-template UI branching.
Future reference systems that compose existing capabilities require profile registration/configuration but no new Systems page or panel.
A genuinely new interaction primitive still requires a reviewed contract and renderer extension.

consequences: Reference and future authored systems could define novel workflows without application registration.
The current repository does not yet have the sandbox and controlled-environment evidence required for that broader execution authority.
Delivery risk and security scope are materially larger than the requested replacement.
options.label: Release-declared workflow language
options.summary: Compile complete declarative workflow definitions into each release and let a generic interpreter render and execute their typed steps through a capability broker.
tradeoffs: Provides the greatest portability and could eventually support authored workflows.
Requires a new signed workflow language, compiler, interpreter, policy proof, migration/versioning model, sandbox qualification, and substantially broader threat analysis.
Makes release artifacts a larger security-sensitive public contract.

consequences: The page would look more general but retain the same scaling problem internally.
Host parity and denial behavior become harder to prove as plug-ins multiply.
This does not fully satisfy the requested move away from reference-system-specific workflows.
options.label: Renderer workflow plug-ins
options.summary: Keep separate feature components but register them behind profile ids in the shared renderer, selecting one component after release classification.
tradeoffs: Smallest migration and preserves most current UI code.
Still requires a new component and client wiring for each interaction type.
Encourages product and authority decisions to drift into renderer and host composition.

decisions.question: Where should configurable Run & Test workflow definitions and dispatch authority live?
decisions.title: General Run & Test workflow authority

constraints: Replace reference-template and reference-runtime-kind branching with verified capability/profile resolution; adding another reference system that reuses supported capabilities must not require another Run & Test panel.
Use one shared workflow shell and shared bounded interaction primitives for desktop and thin client; host code composes clients and supported handlers without owning product behavior.
Keep design-time asset configuration schemas separate from runtime workflow input contracts and never treat renderer state or inert asset metadata as execution authority.
Resolve every workflow against an exact workspace-owned approved release or reviewed execution plan and an application/host-supported handler before presenting it as runnable.

Workflow discovery and selection are read-only. Approval, deployment, mutation, invocation, retry, and cancellation remain explicit application commands with their existing authorization and integrity checks.

Preserve separate conversation, system-data, system-review, deployment, and execution record families behind the general workflow boundary rather than coercing their persistence models into one record.

Imported or authored executable content remains unavailable without an independently qualified sandbox and explicit host support; unknown profile, handler, capability, schema, or result kinds fail closed.
Lazy-load only the selected workflow and bound input, output, history, diagnostics, and rendered collections.
Implement this successor in economically meaningful increments and run the full suite only after each complete increment, using focused tests for internal chunks.

discovery.summary: Systems Run & Test currently mounts three interaction panels that mirror the three shipped reference-system families, followed by a separate general deployment workflow. The desktop and thin-client pages hard-code those panels, while deployment contracts and runtime adapters also classify releases through a closed SystemReferenceRuntimeKind union. Existing execution-run and runtime-execution contracts provide reusable lifecycle and adapter foundations, but the repository has no application-owned catalog that describes which safe user workflows an exact release supports. A durable design must select workflows from verified release capabilities and host support rather than from reference-template identity or renderer branching.
